newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia welcomes Iraq-U.N. oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia welcomes Iraq-U.N. oil deal.

text.p: King Fahd of Saudi Arabia has welcomed Iraq's acceptance of U.N. terms for limited oil exports, the official Saudi news agency SPA said late on Monday.
It quoted Information Minister Fouad bin Abdul-Salam bin Mohammad Farisi as saying the monarch said the accord would "help end the suffering of the Iraqi people".
The king was speaking during Monday's weekly cabinet meeting, which he chaired.

Iraq last week accepted United Nations terms to implement a deal signed in May allowing it to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to pay for food and medicine and some U.N. operations related to the Gulf crisis.

The U.N. imposed stringent sanctions on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990. Saudi Arabia was home to U.S.-led multinational forces that ended Iraq's seven-month occupation of the Gulf Arab state in February 1991.
Its ties with Iraq have remained strained since the Gulf War.
